rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forbidding alliance with unbelievers, the verse names those truly worthy of it: God is the original guardian, while the Messenger and believers hold that role dependently.
rows.anchor: لما نهى عن موالاة الكفرة ذكر عقيبه من هو حقيق بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer and almsgiving clauses modify the believers as an adjective or stand in apposition; they may also be accusative or nominative as praise.
rows.anchor: صفة للذين آمنوا فإنه جرى مجرى الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred sense is that they are humble in their prayer and almsgiving.
rows.anchor: متخشعون في صلاتهم وزكاتهم، وقيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative ties the phrase to giving alms while bowing in prayer, out of eagerness to do good.
rows.anchor: في حال ركوعهم في الصلاة حرصا على الإحسان ومسارعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says it was revealed about ʿAlī: a petitioner asked him for help as he prayed, and he gave the petitioner his ring.
rows.anchor: نزلت في علي رضي الله عنه حين سأله سائل وهو راكع

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: الشيعة
rows.claim: The Shiʿites cite the verse for ʿAlī’s imamate, taking walī to mean the one who governs affairs and is entitled to exercise authority.
rows.anchor: استدل بها الشيعة على إمامته زاعمين أن المراد بالولي

words: إِنَّمَا وَلِيُّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is the one given above, and reading a plural as one person is also nonapparent; if revealed about ʿAlī, the plural may invite others to emulate him.
rows.anchor: والظاهر ما ذكرناه مع أن حمل الجمع على الواحد أيضا خلاف الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this interpretation, a small action during prayer does not invalidate it, and voluntary charity can be called zakāh.
rows.anchor: الفعل القليل في الصلاة لا يبطلها وأن صدقة التطوع تسمى زكاة

words: وَمَن يَتَوَلَّ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking God, the Messenger, and believers as allies is the sense of taking them as patrons.
rows.anchor: ومن يتخذهم أولياء. { فإن حزب الله هم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit “God’s party” replaces a pronoun to spell out the proof, honor the group, and imply that allies of others belong to Satan’s party.
rows.anchor: فهم حزب الله وحزب الله هم الغالبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥizb is a group assembled for a matter that has confronted or occupied them.
rows.anchor: وأصل الحزب القوم يجتمعون لأمر حز بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition was revealed concerning Rifāʿa ibn Zayd and Suwayd ibn al-Ḥārith, who professed Islam but were hypocrites and whom some Muslims befriended.
rows.anchor: نزلت في رفاعة بن زيد وسويد بن الحرث أظهرا الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mockery of religion explains the prohibition: people of this character are unfit for alliance and deserve enmity.
rows.anchor: إيماء إلى العلة وتنبيها على أن من هذا شأنه

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read al-kuffār in the genitive, separating mockers among the People of the Book from unbelievers; here the term may especially mean polytheists because their unbelief is compounded.
rows.anchor: على قراءة من جره وهم أبو عمرو والكسائي ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading coordinates al-kuffār with those who take the religion in mockery, forbidding alliance with anyone outside the truth, whether scriptural or polytheist.
rows.anchor: ومن نصبه عطفه على الذين اتخذوا على أن النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fearing God means leaving the prohibited acts, as true faith requires; alternatively, the condition means believing God’s promise and threat.
rows.anchor: لأن الإيمان حقا يقتضي ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They come before God for reckoning and recompense.
rows.anchor: للحساب والجزاء. { فرادى } منفردين عن الأموال والأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They arrive alone, separated from possessions, children, and worldly attachments, or from the helpers and idols they claimed would intercede.
rows.anchor: منفردين عن الأموال والأولاد وسائر ما آثرتموه من الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Furādā is a plural of fard, with the final alif marking the feminine plural form.
rows.anchor: وهو جمع فرد والألف للتأنيث ككسالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Variants include furād, compared to rikhāl or thulāth, and fardā, compared to sukrā.
rows.anchor: «فراد» كرخال وفراد كثلاث وفردى كسكرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison may be an appositive, a second circumstantial clause, a circumstance of furādā, or an adjective describing the manner of coming.
rows.anchor: على الهيئة التي ولدتم عليها في الانفراد، أو حال ثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation compares their arrival with first creation: barefoot, unclothed, uncircumcised, and solitary.
rows.anchor: ابتداء خلقكم عراة حفاة غرلا بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God bestowed in worldly life distracted them from the afterlife, but they left it behind and carried away nothing, not even a tiny amount.
rows.anchor: ما تفضلنا به عليكم في الدنيا فشغلتم به عن الآخرة

words: شُفَعَآءَكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ أَنَّهُمْ فِيكُمْ شُرَكَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged partners were claimed to share God’s lordship over them and their entitlement to worship.
rows.anchor: شفعاءكم الذين زعمتم أنهم فيكم شركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means their bond has been severed and their gathering scattered; bayn can mean connection or separation.
rows.anchor: أي تقطع وصلكم وتشتت جمعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, bayn is an adverb made subject to the verb by extension, meaning severance occurred among them.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو ظرف أسند إليه الفعل اتساعا

rows.speaker: نافع والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: They read baynakum in the accusative with an omitted agent inferred from what precedes; another attested form supplies mā before baynakum.
rows.anchor: قراءة نافع والكسائي وحفص عن عاصم بالنصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim was either that idols would intercede for them or that there would be no resurrection and recompense.
rows.anchor: ما كنتم تزعمون } أنها شفعاؤكم أو أن لا بعث ولا جزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording refers to creating Adam as clay before forming him; his creation counts as creation of humanity, or humanity began through Adam.
rows.anchor: خلقنا أباكم آدم طينا غير مصور ثم صورناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle thumma may signal a delay in the telling rather than in the events.
rows.anchor: وقيل ثم لتأخير الإخبار. { فسجدوا إلا إبليس

words: فَسَجَدُوا۟ إِلَّآ إِبْلِيسَ لَمْ يَكُن مِّنَ ٱلسَّٰجِدِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis was excluded because he was not among those who prostrated to Adam.
rows.anchor: فسجدوا إلا إبليس لم يكن من السجدين } ممن سجد لآدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra lā reinforces the verb and highlights the censured omission; alternatively, the question asks what forced Iblis not to prostrate.
rows.anchor: ولا صلة مثلها في لئلا يعلم، مؤكدة معنى الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is evidence that an unqualified command entails obligation and immediacy.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن مطلق الأمر للوجوب والفور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis considered himself superior and could not imagine a superior being ordered to bow to an inferior; he originated arrogance and rational good-and-evil doctrine.
rows.anchor: هو الذي سن التكبر وقال بالحسن والقبح العقليين أولا

words: خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍۢ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis wrongly measured merit by material origin, ignoring direct creation, form, and purpose; Adam’s knowledge and distinctive qualities explain the command to bow.
rows.anchor: بأن رأى الفضل كله باعتبار العنصر وغفل عما يكون باعتبار الفاعل

words: خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍۢ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage indicates generation and corruption and that devils are created bodies; Adam’s clay and Satan’s fire may be their dominant constituents.
rows.anchor: دليل الكون والفساد وأن الشياطين أجسام كائنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madhmūm means blamed, from the verb meaning to blame; variants ease or alter its hamza.
rows.anchor: مذموما من ذأمه إذا ذمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One variant is compared to masʾūl and another to makīl; the lexeme is also explained through dhāma-yadhīmuhu-dhayman.
rows.anchor: كمسول في مسؤول أو كمكول في مكيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madhḥūr means driven away.
rows.anchor: مذموما مدحورا } مطرودا. { لمن تبعك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām marks an oath, answered by “I will fill”; that answer also serves as the conditional answer.
rows.anchor: اللام فيه لتوطئة القسم وجوابه: { لأملأن جهنم منكم أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With kasra on the lām, the phrase may predicate the threat or give a cause for expulsion; “I will fill” then answers an unspoken oath, and “you” includes them by predominance.
rows.anchor: بكسر اللام على أنه خبر لأملأن على معنى: لمن تبعك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied wording is “And We said: O Adam.”
rows.anchor: أي وقلنا يا آدم. { اسكن أنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variant hādhī is described as original from the diminutive dhayyā, with hāʾ substituted for yāʾ.
rows.anchor: هذي وهو الأصل لتصغيره على ذيا والهاء بدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning means they would become people who wronged themselves.
rows.anchor: فتصيرا من الذين ظلموا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takūnā may be jussive by coordination or subjunctive as the consequence of the prohibition.
rows.anchor: وتكونا يحتمل الجزم على العطف والنصب على الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waswasa is a quiet, hidden sound like murmuring or rustling, as in the sound of jewelry; its manner is discussed in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وهي في الأصل الصوت الخفي كالهينمة والخشخشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām can mark the outcome or purpose; Satan also intended their distress at being exposed, hence the word “shame.”
rows.anchor: واللام للعاقبة أو للغرض على أنه أراد أيضا

words: لِيُبْدِىَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِىَ عَنْهُمَا مِن سَوْءَٰتِهِمَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What had been covered was their private parts; neither saw them on themselves or one another.
rows.anchor: ما غطي عنهما من عوراتهما، وكانا لا يريانها من أنفسهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage indicates that uncovering one’s nakedness in private, even before a spouse, is naturally regarded as ugly without need.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن كشف العورة في الخلوة وعند الزوج من غير حاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One variant drops the hamza and transfers its vowel to wāw; another changes hamza to wāw and assimilates the two wāws. The usual form retains it because the second wāw is long.
rows.anchor: بحذف الهمزة وإلقاء حركتها على الواو و سوأتهما بقلبها واوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s claim means the prohibition was out of dislike that they become angels.
rows.anchor: إلا كراهة أن تكونا. { ملكين أو تكونا من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The immortal ones are those who do not die or remain eternally in Paradise.
rows.anchor: الذين لا يموتون أو يخلدون في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inference that angels outrank prophets is rejected: Adam and Eve sought angelic innate qualities and freedom from food and drink, not absolute superiority.
rows.anchor: أنه كان من المعلوم أن الحقائق لا تنقلب وإنما كانت رغبتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal form of “he swore to them” intensifies the act of swearing.
rows.anchor: أخرجه على زنة المفاعلة للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says they accepted his oath; another says they swore him by God to sincerity, so his answering oath became a mutual exchange.
rows.anchor: وقيل أقسما له بالقبول. وقيل أقسما عليه بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qisṭ is justice, the middle course in every matter, apart from excess and deficiency.
rows.anchor: بالعدل وهو الوسط من كل أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means direct yourselves uprightly to worship without turning elsewhere, or face the qibla.
rows.anchor: وتوجهوا إلى عبادته مستقيمين غير عادلين إلى غيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “At every mosque” can mean each time or place of prostration, namely prayer, or any mosque where prayer finds you, without delaying until return to your own mosque.
rows.anchor: في كل وقت سجود أو مكانه وهو الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling upon God here means worshipping Him.
rows.anchor: واعبدوه. { مخلصين له الدين } أي الطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dīn means obedience, since all return to God.
rows.anchor: أي الطاعة فإن إليه مصيركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God originated creation, He will recreate people to requite their deeds; likening return to beginning establishes resurrection’s possibility and God’s power, so worship should be sincere.
rows.anchor: وإنما شبه الإعادة بالإبداء تقريرا لإمكانها والقدرة عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views say people return to soil, in their first naked and barefoot state, or as believers and unbelievers as first created.
rows.anchor: وقيل كما بدأكم من التراب تعودون إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rajfa was an earthquake; al-Ḥijr calls it a cry, which may have been the earthquake’s onset.
rows.anchor: الزلزلة وفي سورة «الحجر» فأخذتهم الصيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their dār means their town or city.
rows.anchor: في دارهم جثمين } أي في مدينتهم

words: ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ شُعَيْبًۭا كَأَن لَّمْ يَغْنَوْا۟ فِيهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first relative clause is a subject whose predicate is “as though they had never lived there”; maghnā means a dwelling place.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ خبره { كأن لم يغنوا فيها }

words: ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ شُعَيْبًۭا كَأَن لَّمْ يَغْنَوْا۟ فِيهَا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were uprooted as if they had never lived there; maghnā means a dwelling place.
rows.anchor: أي استؤصلوا كأن لم يقيموا بها والمغنى المنزل

words: ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ شُعَيْبًۭا كَانُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلْخَٰسِرِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers lost in religion and worldly life; those who believed and followed Shuʿayb, despite the deniers’ claim, gained in both abodes.
rows.anchor: دينا ودنيا لا الذين صدقوه واتبعوه كما زعموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the relative clause and using two independent nominal sentences emphasizes this reversal.
rows.anchor: كرر الموصول واستأنف بالجملتين وأتى بهما اسميتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God dispersed them across the earth in communities, leaving scarcely any region without them, to prevent them regaining collective strength.
rows.anchor: وفرقناهم فيها بحيث لا يكاد يخلو قطر منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umaman may be a second object or a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: أمما } مفعول ثان أو حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some are below the righteous in rank: their unbelievers and disobedient members.
rows.anchor: تقديره ومنهم أناس دون ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good and bad with which they were tested are blessings and afflictions.
rows.anchor: بالحسنت والسيئات } بالنعم والنقم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tests aim to make them stop and turn back from their conduct.
rows.anchor: لعلهم يرجعون } ينهون فيرجعون عما كانوا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalf means a bad successor; as a verbal noun used adjectivally it can refer to one or many, though it is also treated as a collective noun.
rows.anchor: خلف } بدل سوء مصدر نعت به ولذلك يقع على الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They inherited the Torah from their ancestors, reading it and knowing what it contained.
rows.anchor: التوراة من أسلافهم يقرؤونها ويقفون على ما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This lowly worldly gain may be called near or base; it refers to bribes in judgment and payment for distorting words.
rows.anchor: حطام هذا الشيء الأدنى يعني الدنيا، وهو من الدنو أو الدناءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They say, ‘We will be forgiven’” may coordinate with the prior verb or be circumstantial; the verb may be construed with the prepositional phrase or as a verbal noun of their taking.
rows.anchor: سيغفر لنا } لا يؤاخذنا الله بذلك ويتجاوز عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They expect forgiveness while persisting in sin and returning to the same conduct without repentance.
rows.anchor: يرجون المغفرة مصرين على الذنب عائدين إلى مثله غير تائبين عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The covenant was in the Book; its truth requirement rebukes their certainty of forgiveness without repentance as a lie and breach of the covenant.
rows.anchor: المراد توبيخهم على البت بالمغفرة مع عدم التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They studied what it contained” may coordinate semantically with the covenant question, or with inheriting the Book as an aside.
rows.anchor: عطف على { ألم يؤخذ } من حيث المعنى فإنه تقرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is better for the pious than these people’s gains; they should not exchange a base worldly prize that brings punishment for lasting bliss.
rows.anchor: ولا يستبدلوا الأدنى الدنيء المؤدي إلى العقاب

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وحفص ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read the verb with tāʾ, shifting the grammatical person.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وحفص ويعقوب بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who hold to the Book may coordinate with the God-fearing; alternatively they begin a sentence promising not to waste the reformers’ reward, or replace an implicit pronoun to stress reform.
rows.anchor: عطف على الذين { يتقون } وقوله: { أفلا يعقلون } اعتراض

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr reads yumsikūn lightly; prayer uses a singular verb because it surpasses other forms of adherence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر { يمسكون } بالتخفيف وإفراد الإقامة

words: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them means worshipping them and naming them gods.
rows.anchor: تدعون من دون الله } أي تعبدونهم وتسمونهم آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are servants like humans in being owned and subjected.
rows.anchor: من حيث إنها مملوكة مسخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the idols really are gods, call them and see whether they can answer.
rows.anchor: فادعوهم فليستجيبوا لكم إن كنتم صدقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, carved in human form, their utmost status would be living rational beings like their worshippers, who are no more entitled to worship one another.
rows.anchor: لما نحتوها بصور الأناسي قال لهم: إن قصارى أمرهم

words: أَلَهُمْ أَرْجُلٌۭ يَمْشُونَ بِهَآ أَمْ لَهُمْ أَيْدٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant lightens inna and puts ʿibād in the accusative, treating the particle as a negation like Ḥijāzī mā; the author says this construction is unattested.
rows.anchor: بتخفيف { أن } ونصب { عباد } على أنها نافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yabṭishūn is read with ḍamma here and in al-Qaṣaṣ and al-Dukhān.
rows.anchor: { يبطشون } بالضم ها هنا وفي «القصص»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He challenges them to summon their alleged partners and enlist them in hostility toward him.
rows.anchor: ادعوا شركاءكم } واستعينوا بهم في عداوتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He challenges them to use every available stratagem without delay.
rows.anchor: فبالغوا فيما تقدرون عليه من مكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He fears nothing because he trusts in God’s guardianship and protection.
rows.anchor: فلا تمهلون فإني لا أبالي بكم لوثوقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance privately covers recitation, supplication, and other forms; al-Shāfiʿī takes it as quiet recitation by a congregant after the imam finishes.
rows.anchor: عام في الأذكار من القراءة والدعاء وغيرهما

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī applies the command to a congregant reciting quietly after the imam finishes.
rows.anchor: كما هو مذهب الشافعي رضي الله تعالى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshipper is humble and fearful, speaking above a whisper but below a raised voice, which supports humility and sincerity.
rows.anchor: فوق السر ودون الجهر فإنه أدخل في الخشوع والإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase refers to morning and evening times.
rows.anchor: بالغدو والأصال } بأوقات الغدو والعشيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads al-īṣāl, the verbal noun for entering late afternoon, matching the morning term.
rows.anchor: «والايصال» وهو مصدر آصل إذا دخل في الأصيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is against being heedless of God’s remembrance.
rows.anchor: ولا تكن من الغفلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those near their Lord are the angels of the highest assembly.
rows.anchor: إن الذين عند ربك } يعني ملائكة الملأ الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not disdain worship and declare God’s transcendence.
rows.anchor: لا يستكبرون عن عبادته ويسبحونه } وينزهونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prostration is exclusive worship and submission to God, without associating anything with Him.
rows.anchor: وله يسجدون } ويخصونه بالعبادة والتذلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ conduct reproaches other accountable beings, and prostration is prescribed when this verse is recited.
rows.anchor: وهو تعريض بمن عداهم من المكلفين ولذلك شرع السجود

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says Satan withdraws weeping when a human recites a prostration verse and prostrates, since the human obeyed and earns Paradise while Satan disobeyed and earns Fire.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says reciting Sūrat al-Aʿrāf earns a screen between the reciter and Iblis on Judgment Day, with Adam interceding for the reciter.
rows.anchor: وعنه صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees are Abū Sufyān and his companions; “say to them” means “say for their sake.”
rows.anchor: يعني أبا سفيان وأصحابه والمعنى قل لأجلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they stop opposing the Messenger by entering Islam, their past sins will be forgiven.
rows.anchor: عن معاداة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بالدخول في الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Variants with tāʾ and kāf address the unbelievers directly; another reads an active verb with God as its subject.
rows.anchor: بالتاء والكاف على أنه خاطبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they return to fighting, expect the precedent of earlier groups who united against prophets and were destroyed, as at Badr.
rows.anchor: كما جرى على أهل بدر فليتوقعوا مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fitna means the absence of polytheism; the religion belongs wholly to God when false religions disappear.
rows.anchor: لا تكون فتنة } لا يوجد فيهم شرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they stop unbelief, God sees their conduct and recompenses their conversion.
rows.anchor: فيجازيهم على انتهائهم عنه وإسلامهم

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads the verb in the second person, addressing believers about jihad, calling to Islam, and bringing people from unbelief’s darkness to faith’s light.
rows.anchor: وعن يعقوب «تعملون» بالتاء على معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tying the condition to unbelievers stopping implies reward for their direct change and for fighters who cause it.
rows.anchor: كما يستدعي إثابتهم للمباشرة يستدعي إثابة مقاتليهم للتسبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hypocrite men and women resemble one another in hypocrisy and distance from faith, like parts of one thing.
rows.anchor: متشابهة في النفاق والبعد عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, this rebuts their oath that they belong to believers and confirms they do not; their conduct demonstrates the opposition.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه تكذيب لهم في حلفهم بالله إنهم لمنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They command unbelief and sins and forbid faith and obedience.
rows.anchor: وينهون عن المعروف } عن الإيمان والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Withholding their hands is an idiom for miserliness.
rows.anchor: وقبض اليد كناية عن الشح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They neglected remembrance of God and obedience to Him.
rows.anchor: غفلوا عن ذكر الله وتركوا طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s “forgetting” means withholding His favor and grace.
rows.anchor: فتركهم من لطفه وفضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are fully given to rebellion and departure from the sphere of good.
rows.anchor: الكاملون في التمرد والفسوق عن دائرة الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises hypocrites and unbelievers lasting confinement in Hell; its sufficiency as punishment shows its severity.
rows.anchor: مقدرين الخلود. { هي حسبهم } عقابا وجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s curse removes them from mercy and humiliates them; lasting punishment may mean Hell or the hardship of hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: لا ينقطع والمراد به ما وعدوه أو ما يقاسونه من تعب النفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers’ mutual guardianship contrasts with the hypocrites’ mutual affiliation in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: في مقابلة قوله المنافقون والمنافقات بعضهم من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers promote right, oppose wrong, pray, give alms, and obey God and His Messenger in all other matters.
rows.anchor: ويطيعون الله ورسوله } في سائر الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The future particle sīn emphasizes that God’s mercy for them will certainly occur.
rows.anchor: لا محالة فإن السين مؤكدة للوقوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is sovereign over everything and nothing He wills can resist Him; He is wise, placing things where they belong.
rows.anchor: { حكيم } يضع الأشياء مواضعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God gave them from His bounty, they withheld the due owed to Him.
rows.anchor: بخلوا به } منعوا حق الله منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They turned away from obedience and were habitually averse to it.
rows.anchor: وهم قوم عادتهم الإعراض عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their action brought hypocrisy and corrupt belief into their hearts; alternatively, “their” refers to stinginess that settled hypocrisy there.
rows.anchor: فجعل الله عاقبة فعلهم ذلك نفاقا وسوء اعتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day they meet Him can mean death, or meeting their deed and recompense on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: يلقون الله بالموت أو يلقون عملهم أي جزاءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment follows breaking a promise of charity and righteousness; a broken promise entails lying and is blameworthy on both counts.
rows.anchor: بسبب إخلافهم ما وعدوه من التصدق والصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads yukadhdhibūn with gemination.
rows.anchor: مستقبح من الوجهين أو المقال مطلقا وقرىء { يكذبون } بالتشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied subject may be hypocrites or those who made a covenant with God; a variant shifts to direct address with tāʾ.
rows.anchor: أي المنافقون أو من عاهد الله وقرىء بالتاء على الالتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their secret is inward hypocrisy or an intention to break their promise.
rows.anchor: ما أسروه في أنفسهم من النفاق أو العزم على الإخلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their private conversations contain attacks among themselves or their labeling zakāh a jizya.
rows.anchor: وما يتناجون به فيما بينهم من المطاعن، أو تسمية الزكاة جزية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows unseen things, so none of this is hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: علم الغيوب } فلا يخفى عليه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that when released, they offered the wealth left behind and asked the Prophet to give it as charity and purify them; he replied he was not commanded to take their money, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: قالوا يا رسول الله هذه أموالنا التي خلفتنا فتصدق بها وطهرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The charity purifies them from sins or attachment to wealth that could lead them to repeat the misconduct.
rows.anchor: من الذنوب أو حب المال المؤدي بهم إلى مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One variant derives the verb from a form meaning “purify”; another makes it jussive as a response to the command.
rows.anchor: تطهرهم } من أطهره بمعنى طهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes the verb jussive as response to the imperative.
rows.anchor: و { تطهرهم } بالجزم جوابا للأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through charity God increases their good deeds and raises them to the ranks of the sincere.
rows.anchor: وتنمي بها حسناتهم وترفعهم إلى منازل المخلصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pray for them by showing care and asking forgiveness on their behalf.
rows.anchor: واعطف عليهم بالدعاء والاستغفار لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s prayer settles their souls and reassures their hearts; its plural reflects multiple recipients.
rows.anchor: تسكن إليها نفوسهم وتطمئن بها قلوبهم

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read the word in the singular.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears their confession and knows their remorse.
rows.anchor: والله سميع } لاعترافهم. { عليم } بندامتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny proof out of extreme obstinacy and disregard even the miracles brought to them.
rows.anchor: بحجة تدل على صحة دعواك وهو لفرط عنادهم

words: وَمَا نَحْنُ بِتَارِكِىٓ ءَالِهَتِنَا عَن قَوْلِكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They refuse to abandon their idols’ worship at Hud’s word; the phrase describes their state as they refuse.
rows.anchor: صادرين عن قولك حال من الضمير في تاركي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their words are meant to make Hud despair of their response or belief.
rows.anchor: إقناط له من الإجابة والتصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They claim some gods afflicted him with madness for insulting them and turning people away; the root means to be afflicted, and they portray his speech as ravings.
rows.anchor: أي أصابك من عراه يعروه إذا أصابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is their saying’s content; illā is redundant because the exception is already exhaustive.
rows.anchor: والجملة مقول القول وإلا لغو لأن الاستثناء مفرغ

words: إِنِّىٓ أُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ وَٱشْهَدُوٓا۟ أَنِّى بَرِىٓءٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud calls God and them to witness that he is clear of their association of partners and idols.
rows.anchor: بأن أشهد الله تعالى على براءته من آلهتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He contemptuously tells them to unite and try to kill him without delay; if they fail, they must concede their lifeless idols cannot harm him.
rows.anchor: وأن يجتمعوا على الكيد في إهلاكه من غير إنظار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His bold challenge before a fierce crowd is a miracle grounded in trust in God, while their failure to hurt him shows divine protection.
rows.anchor: فإن مواجهة الواحد الجم الغفير من الجبابرة الفتاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account leads into Hud’s explanation that trust in God makes threats powerless.
rows.anchor: ليس إلا لثقته بالله وتثبطهم عن إضراره ليس إلا بعصمته إياه ولذلك عقبه بقوله

words: إِنِّى تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ رَبِّى وَرَبِّكُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hud trusts God’s protection: God owns both Hud and them, so they cannot harm him except by what God wills or decrees.
rows.anchor: أنكم وإن بذلتم غاية وسعكم لن تضروني

words: مَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ ءَاخِذٌۢ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God owns every creature and can direct it as He wills; taking a creature by its forelock is a metaphor for this control.
rows.anchor: إلا وهو مالك لها قادر عليها يصرفها على ما يريد بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is just and true: no one who seeks refuge with Him is lost, and no wrongdoer escapes Him.
rows.anchor: على الحق والعدل لا يضيع عنده معتصم ولا يفوته ظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rescued Ṣāliḥ and the believers by grace from the day’s humiliation, either destruction by the cry or disgrace on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: نجيناهم من خزي يومئذ وهو هلاكهم بالصيحة

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ reads yawmaʾidhin with fatḥa by transfer of the genitive construction’s case ending; the same occurs in al-Maʿārij.
rows.anchor: وعن نافع { يومئذ } بالفتح على اكتساب المضاف البناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is capable of everything and overcomes all.
rows.anchor: القادر على كل شيء والغالب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of the cry and crouching was already explained in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
rows.anchor: قد سبق تفسير ذلك في سورة «الأعراف»

rows.speaker: أبو بكر والكسائي وابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Authorities vary in tanwīn on Thamūd here, in al-Najm, and in the later curse; the choice treats the name as the tribe or founding ancestor.
rows.anchor: نونه أبو بكر ها هنا وفي «النجم» والكسائي في جميع القرآن وابن كثير ونافع وابن عامر وأبو عمرو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madyan may mean the descendants of Madyan son of Abraham or the town he built and named for himself.
rows.anchor: أولاد مدين بن إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it refers to the town’s inhabitants.
rows.anchor: أو أهل مدين وهو بلد بناه فسمي باسمه

words: ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He begins with monotheism as the foundation, then forbids short measure and weight as unjust and destructive of fair exchange.
rows.anchor: ثم نهاهم عما اعتادوه من البخس المنافي للعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prosperity makes cheating unnecessary; alternatively it is a blessing calling for generosity, or abundance they should not forfeit through wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أراكم بخير } بسعة تغنيكم عن البخس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment leaves none outside it; it may be a destructive punishment, meaning Judgment Day or extermination.
rows.anchor: لا يشذ منه أحد منكم. وقيل عذاب مهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is called encompassing although this attribute belongs to its punishment, because the day contains it.
rows.anchor: ووصف اليوم بالإحاطة وهي صفة العذاب لاشتماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mock his monotheistic message and prayer, suggesting his call has no rational motive and comes from the fancies of someone devoted to prayer.
rows.anchor: على الاستهزاء به والتهكم بصلواته والإشعار بأن مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb prayed frequently, explaining why they used the plural and singled prayer out for mockery.
rows.anchor: وكان شعيب كثير الصلاة فلذلك جمعوا وخصوا الصلاة بالذكر

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read “your prayer” in the singular.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص على الإفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the singular reading, the prayer commands them to leave; a genitive noun is omitted because a man does not command another’s action.
rows.anchor: فحذف المضاف لأن الرجل لا يؤمر بفعل غيره

words: أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may coordinate with their ancestors’ worship, meaning “or leave doing as we wish with wealth”; a tāʾ reading coordinates with “that we leave” and answers the prohibition on cheating and command to give full measure.
rows.anchor: عطف على ما أي وأن نترك فعلنا ما نشاء في أموالنا

words: أَوْ أَن نَّفْعَلَ فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِنَا مَا نَشَٰٓؤُا۟
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant uses tāʾ in both verbs, coordinating with “that we leave” as the response to the ban on cheating and the command to give full measure.
rows.anchor: بالتاء فيهما على أن العطف على { أن نترك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say Shuʿayb forbade clipping dirhams and dinars, which is what they meant by freedom with their money.
rows.anchor: كان ينهاهم عن تقطيع الدراهم والدنانير فأرادوا به ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They sarcastically describe him as the opposite of forbearing and rightly guided, or claim his good sense should restrain such exhortations.
rows.anchor: تهكموا به وقصدوا وصفه بضد ذلك
